identity.cta_id: Stable, language-independent semantic identity assigned in reviewed mapping. Never derive from CSS classes, DOM position or rendered copy.
identity.cta_name: Reviewed human-readable reporting label; separate from identity and translated rendered text.
identity.cta_location: Explicit semantic placement, such as nav, hero, platform, earnings, footer or a named new section.
identity.cta_section: Required stable semantic section token, using lowercase letters/numbers separated by hyphens or underscores; never derive from rendered headings.
identity.cta_version: Explicit revision for the existing CTA's wording, design or behavior. Assigned by the author; never guessed from CSS or text.
identity.page_name: Reviewed reporting label authored as data-page-name on html or body. Never derive from document.title, headings, paths or user input. Missing or invalid labels remain null.
identity.page_version: Explicit page/template revision authored as data-page-version on html or body. An existing html attribute takes precedence over body. Never infer or automatically increment it at runtime.
identity.release_version: Explicit page/release revision. A new section changes the page/release revision even when existing CTAs are untouched.
identity.tracking_schema_version: Revision of the event property contract, independent of CTA and page/release versions.
identity.experiment_variant: Separately preserved, reviewed experiment metadata; never inferred from visual styling.

change_rules.change: Add a new section with a new CTA
change_rules.rule: Assign a new semantic cta_id and explicit cta_location, begin cta_version at 1, and advance the page/release version. Add a mapping row and validate event/action/destination. Do not reuse an existing CTA ID merely because the button looks the same.

change_rules.change: Change existing CTA wording or design
change_rules.rule: Preserve cta_id, increment explicit cta_version and advance the page/release version. Update the reviewed human-readable name where appropriate. Keep experiment assignment separately.

Make and record a placement/mapping decision. A genuinely new semantic CTA placement gets its own ID and explicit location, with CTA version starting at 1. Repositioning within the same semantic placement, or redesigning the section around the same CTA, preserves its ID and increments its explicit version. Unchanged CSS does not prove unchanged placement.

change_rules.change: Add a second CTA to an existing section
change_rules.rule: Assign a distinct semantic ID, including a meaningful role suffix if needed. Never distinguish buttons by ordinal DOM index.

future_section_onboarding: Decide whether this is a new logical CTA or a revision/move of an existing one; document the decision in the mapping.

Assign reviewed data-cta-id, data-cta-name, data-cta-location, data-cta-section, data-cta-action and data-cta-version together on the actual interactive anchor; author data-page-name and data-page-version on the page body or preserve an existing reviewed html contract. The delegated handler covers anchors, including anchors styled as buttons; other element types need implementation review.

Validate action against exact destination host/path. Patient direct signup uses Get Started Clicked with direct-signup; directory navigation remains separately labeled; privacy/settings emits no patient signup event. Preserve existing Dietitian Apply Clicked IDs and event name.
Use the existing single delegated handler. Do not add per-button listeners or another tracking embed.
Validate desktop/mobile, nested click targets, keyboard activation, dynamic insertions and repeated initialization, with exactly one event per intended action and consent respected.

Check sanitized payload properties and SDK context; never include raw query strings or form values. After isolated staging publication, verify uniquely QA-marked events in Amplitude rather than relying on browser dispatch alone.

cms_and_component_propagation.template_attributes: Attributes authored on the CTA in a CMS Collection Template propagate to each rendered item page using that template. The template's semantic CTA ID may be shared across those pages; page_path distinguishes the source page. Likewise reused global nav/footer CTAs retain stable role IDs while every event includes distinct page_path, locale and explicit page/release context. Do not manufacture IDs from item names or personal content.
cms_and_component_propagation.collection_lists: Repeated cards from one template can share a template CTA role ID when that is the intended reporting identity. If distinguishing content items is required, add a separately reviewed nonpersonal content identifier; do not encode freeform CMS copy into cta_id.
cms_and_component_propagation.components: Attributes set on a shared component definition propagate to instances unless overridden or bound differently. A component used in several semantic placements needs explicit instance props/bindings for placement and identity; a single hard-coded hero/footer label must not spread to every instance.
cms_and_component_propagation.versions: Increment explicit template/component CTA revision when changing its CTA wording/design/behavior; document affected consumers. Page-specific overrides require their own explicit revision/mapping. Do not assume changing a global release reference alone establishes every page's CTA version.
cms_and_component_propagation.verification: Inspect rendered attributes on at least representative item pages and shared-component instances, including dynamic content and mobile variants. Compare IDs, placement and revision with the mapping. Propagation behavior is proposed authoring guidance; it has not been implemented or verified across this Nourish site.

deployment_state: The coordinating acceptance audit confirms production already receives Dietitian Directory Clicked with release cta-cleanup-2026-10-22-1 and schema 2. This PR's current code identifies itself as cta-cleanup-2026-10-26-1 and has not been published by this work. Updating this draft PR does not deploy, merge or establish a new production cutoff. Preserve the separate existing directory event without dual sending.
rollout: The current draft uses release_version=cta-cleanup-2026-10-26-1 and tracking_schema_version=2. The earlier draft release was cta-cleanup-2026-10-22-1. Neither a PR update nor staging-only rollout establishes a production cutoff. Existing Get Started funnels historically included directory clicks; compare new direct signup separately and use directory event -> Provider Directory Loaded for the directory journey. No dual sending.

implementation_notes.placement_migration: Existing inspected markup is mapped through an explicit finite selector table to declared semantic IDs. Selectors locate markup; IDs/versions are never computed from CSS/text. New placements should use authored data-cta-* attributes. Unannotated genuine signup text links remain tracked with cta_mapping_status=unmapped.
implementation_notes.authored_validation: Author all six patient fields (id, name, location, section, action, version) together and validate rendered attributes before publication. Any authored contract field requires a complete valid patient contract matching the destination action. Empty/missing fields or an apply-dietitian action on a patient destination emit no event. Only completely unauthored patient links retain reviewed migration/unmapped fallback. The older partial-contract fallback exceptions are closed in this draft.
implementation_notes.signup_origins: Patient signup and directory events accept only HTTPS signup.nourish.com and signup.usenourish.com on the standard HTTPS port, without embedded credentials. Insecure origins and alternate ports are not reviewed signup endpoints; navigation is never prevented.
implementation_notes.chart_validation: The sanitized click url intentionally omits queries. Legacy assertions that url contains utm_source cannot validate this contract. Keep existing navigation attribution, validate its allowed parameters offline, and migrate chart assertions only to verified supported user-attribution or FlowLoaded categorical fields. Do not restore raw queries or add duplicate click events to satisfy a legacy chart. Chart inventory and edits are owned separately.
implementation_notes.dietitian_revisions: Keep the four existing Dietitian Apply Clicked IDs, names, legacy element labels and hero/earnings/platform/footer placements. Optional data-cta-section and data-cta-version are validated when authored; absent values retain the location token and version 1. Explicit empty/invalid values emit no event. Earnings remains calculator engagement, not proof of application start.
implementation_notes.local_directory_redirect: Only the verified HTTPS www.nourish.com/find-a-provider route is additionally classified as directory-navigation. Preserve its original href without adding signup attribution parameters. Destination fields describe the clicked marketing redirect, not its eventual signup destination. Other hosts, paths and trailing-slash variants require routing review. Directory taxonomy remains provisional.
implementation_notes.page_version: Read explicit data-page-name and data-page-version from html with body fallback only when the html attribute is absent. Missing/invalid metadata remains null; labels are never inferred from titles, headings or paths. release_version identifies the code revision independently from page/CTA revisions. See cta-browser-handoff.json for the finite draft authoring matrix and preservation rules.
implementation_notes.metadata_safety: CTA events bypass broad UTM enrichment to prevent arbitrary persisted UTM_* properties reappearing. Navigation attribution rewriting remains preserved; unrelated event enrichment is unchanged. URLs and SDK page/tab/referrer context omit query/hash. No raw form values are read.
implementation_notes.historical_compatibility: Legacy property keys remain. Dietitian element labels, IDs and cta_location values remain. Patient element labels now use semantic IDs. Directory navigation sends only Dietitian Directory Clicked. Existing historical Get Started charts are not rewritten and need explicit release-aware comparison.
